Both output files are written and verified. Summary of the analysis:

**Setup**: The dataset is one daily NetCDF file per day (`sst_YYYYMMDD.nc`, version 202506) with `analysed_sst` in kelvin (land = NaN). The region maps to a 60×60 block of 0.02° grid cells (lat 57.42–58.60, lon 18.70–19.88); all 4120 needed daily files (4028 baseline/extension days, 92 target days) were present and read with verified timestamps.

**Method followed exactly**: Sea cells = 3309 cells finite on every target day. Per-cell/day-of-year thresholds (90th percentile, Hazen/type-5) and climatologies (mean) from ±5-calendar-day sliding windows over the baseline, with the 1991-12-27…1991-12-31 and 2003-01-01…2003-01-05 extension days included, 29-Feb values in their calendar neighbours' windows, day 60 filled as the mean of days 59/61, then both smoothed with the wrap-around centred 31-day moving mean — all in float64. Verified by brute-force per-cell/slot recomputation from raw files (bitwise match) and unit tests of the smoother and run detector.

**Result**: **No regional MHW events.** Hot days (SST ≥ threshold) totalled 1727 cell-days, but the longest consecutive hot run in any cell was 4 days, so no per-cell MHW (≥5 days) ever formed, hence no active days. A broad regional warm spell (2004-08-07…08-12, up to 1019 cells hot simultaneously on 2004-08-08, and a smaller 4-day spell in early June) peaked just below the thresholds — which are inflated by the record early-August-2002 Baltic warm spell inside the baseline pool. This is documented in the report's caveats; `complete: true`.
